lina: Hey team — saw a tenant on Dedicated hit 429s even though their Reserved throughput + burst credits should cover it. Console showed reserved usage at ~70% and burst credits at ~80% available. Anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:
omar: Hmm. Is this on a single-node placement or spread? We have node-level isolation that sometimes preempts tenant burst when node is at soft cap.
lina: Single node (pinned tenant). We bumped their reserved to handle steady load, but occasional spikes still get 429s for ~20s windows. Logs show `quota.enforce(): deny(rs=0.8, burst=0.3)` repeated.
kehinde: Can you paste the raw log lines? there was a recent change in the front-proxy that enforces per-key limits before node fairshare. Could be ordering problem.
lina: Paste: ```2026-03-17T14:02:11Z quota.enforce tenant=t-123 key=k-abc node=n12 reserved=2500 rps_used=1800 burst_tokens=120 allow=false reason=NODE_SOFT_LIMIT```
sam: That reason is telling: NODE_SOFT_LIMIT. Means the node's soft cap triggered before tenant-level burst was considered. The scheduler is doing local fairness to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
omar: Right — we intentionally made node soft cap check happen early to protect other tenants on shared nodes. But for Dedicated (pinned) tenants we should favor tenant reserved + burst. We may be over-protecting.
kehinde: Two quick ideas: 1) change enforcement order for pinned/dedicated tenants: tenant_quota -> node_soft_cap -> node_hard_cap. 2) expose `node_soft_pressure` metric so we can correlate console 429 spikes with node-level pressure.
lina: +1 on both. UX folks also asked for clearer console UX: show "effective allowance" = min(tenant_reserved + burst, node_available) with a tooltip explaining node pressure. Right now it's ambiguous.
sam: Implementation detail: moving tenant check first means we need to ensure we still don't let a pinned tenant saturate GPU mem/queues. Might need a cheap admission check that consults node inflight and CUDA queue length before allowing large batches.
omar: Agreed. Also add telemetry fields: `throttle_reason` tag (TENANT, NODE_SOFT, NODE_HARD, GLOBAL), `burst_balance` numeric, and `node_inflight` gauge. That will make dashboards actionable.
kehinde: For rollout: feature-flag the enforcement-order change behind `dedicated-prefer-tenant-burst`. Canary on two underutilized dedicated nodes first, monitor `tail_latency` and `node_gpu_util`.
lina: Can we add console annotations when the flag is enabled so SRE can opt-in per-customer? Maybe a toggle in the tenant page "prefer tenant burst on pinned nodes" with a warning about possible node pressure.
sam: Yes — backend flag + console toggle that flips it for that tenant id. We'll log audit events.
omar: I can sketch a patch: modify quota pipeline `check_order` to be dynamic per-tenant: if tenant.pinned && tenant.type==DEDICATED => [TENANT, NODE_SOFT, NODE_HARD] else => [NODE_SOFT, TENANT, NODE_HARD]. Add unit tests around simultaneous requests with high batch sizes.
kehinde: One more edge: cache warmups (KV cache) will spike mem and create transient inflight that still triggers node_soft. We should delay heavy batched requests for X ms post cache-evict or use per-tenant ramping. Add `ramp_window_ms` param to tenant config.
lina: Nice. Action items: Omar — make patch + tests. Sam — add telemetry metrics + node_inflight. Kehinde — update console mock for effective allowance and toggle. I'll coordinate SRE canary and message customers.
omar: Working on it, will open PR and tag @kehinde @sam.
deply-bot: deploy queued: patch/quota-pipeline -> staging (canary nodes). ETA 12m. :eyes:
lina: Thanks! I'll follow up with a short postmortem-style note after canary runs. :+1:
